memory_lessons.applicability: Use this result as a route-level reference, but compare per-size repeated timings before tuning the n=1024 path.
memory_lessons.claim: The previous tiled/OpenMP candidate and baseline were both correct; their reported means were 0.01587444 s and 5.71095333 s respectively. The supplied measurements do not isolate n=1024 performance.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this K-major 4x256x16 candidate against the prior candidate under the same protocol, including repeated native timings for n=1024.

proposal.hypothesis: The only measured T1 variant used 8x128x32 tiles and static row-tile ownership, with a valid reported mean of 0.01587444 s but no per-size timing in the supplied data. This contrasting 4x256x16 variant traverses tiles in row-K-column order; its smaller row group and wider contiguous column tile may improve locality or reduce loop overhead at n=1024. It retains serial execution for n<256 and tests that ordering/tile choice without claiming a speedup.

retained: Replace fixed-size dispatch with generic positive-n GEMM while zeroing the complete output on every call.
Use unpacked i-k-j accumulation in 4-row, 16-K, 256-column tiles, traversed in row-K-column tile order with a contiguous inner output-column loop.
Assign disjoint row tiles using static OpenMP scheduling, clamp the requested worker count to 1..8, and use an explicit serial path below n=256 or when only one worker is requested.
